title: A watercolour and an acrylic paint can carry blue colour differently
original_forecast: Compare dissolved-species coverage with unresolved pigment/binder states. A blue appearance is not evidence that both paints have the same molecular colourant or obey the same optical dilution law.
original_limitations: These named recipes do not represent all watercolours or acrylic paints. Binder film formation, pigment sedimentation and an exact Beer-Lambert law for the opaque sample are not assumed.
lock_qualification: Producer-reported manifest hash; artifact omits raw Cargo.lock bytes.

assessment.model_scope: Equal formulation doses retain dissolved indigo versus an unresolved pigment/binder pool through equal dilution. Persistent colour states differ. The opaque formulation zero at405nm is only absence of an installed molecular-spectrum contribution, not measured transparency or Beer-Lambert behaviour; no pigment sedimentation or binder film law is inferred.
